title: School voucher program on student test scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
• Method: Two-way-fixed-effects Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study robustness check.  
• Why: The voucher program is adopted at one known date (period 4) only in the treated districts, giving a classic stagger-free treatment/control panel structure. We compare the change in test scores for treated districts before vs. after the program to the simultaneous change in control districts.  
• Key assumption: Parallel trends – in the absence of the voucher, the treated and control districts would have evolved similarly over time. (Event-study pre-treatment coefficients are used to probe this assumption.)

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# School voucher program – Difference-in-Differences
# Data path: experiments/exp_b/data/s03_data.csv
############################################################
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Read data
dt <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s03_data.csv")

# 2. Baseline DID with two-way fixed effects
did_mod <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                 data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n=== Baseline DID result ===\n")
print(summary(did_mod)$coefficients)

# 3. Event-study (lead/lag) – reference year = −1 (period 3)
dt[, rel_year := period - 4]                 # years relative to adoption
es_mod <- feols(y ~ i(rel_year, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
                data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n=== Pre-trend test (event-study leads) ===\n")
print(etable(es_mod, keep = "rel_year::[-3:-1]", se = "cluster"))

# Optional plot
ggplot(data = broom::tidy(es_mod),
       aes(x = as.numeric(gsub(".*::", "", term)),
           y = estimate,
           ymin = estimate - 1.96*std.error,
           ymax = estimate + 1.96*std.error)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_pointrange() +
    labs(x = "Years relative to voucher start",
         y = "Coefficient (std. dev. of scores)",
         title = "Event-study for voucher impact") +
    theme_minimal()

# 4. Robustness 1: district-specific linear trends
dt[, t := period]
trend_mod <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post + i(t, unit_id) | unit_id + period,
                   data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n=== DID with district-specific trends ===\n")
print(summary(trend_mod)$coefficients["treat_x_post", ])

# 5. Robustness 2: placebo – pretend the program started in period 2
dt[, placebo_post := as.integer(period >= 2)]
dt[, placebo := treated * placebo_post]
placebo_mod <- feols(y ~ placebo | unit_id + period,
                     data = dt[period < 4], cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n=== Placebo test (pre-periods only) ===\n")
print(summary(placebo_mod)$coefficients)

############################################################
# Key numeric result (baseline DID coefficient)
############################################################
cat("\n=== Main estimate: Voucher effect on test scores ===\n")
cat("beta_hat =", coef(did_mod)["treat_x_post"],
    "\nCluster-robust SE =", se(did_mod, "cluster")["treat_x_post"], "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
• Sign: Positive – vouchers should raise average standardized scores in participating districts.  
• Magnitude: Because `y` is mean-centered (≈ standard-deviation units), an effect of ≈ 0.08 – 0.12 is plausible (roughly one-tenth of a standard deviation, in line with typical educational interventions).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=voucher districts, control=non-voucher; shock=program introduction
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Test scores increase significantly in voucher districts after program launch
